character_sheet: A small ambient butterfly: a one-cube body bar with a one-cube head at the front and four flat wing panels a side — an inner forewing, a larger outer forewing, a hindwing behind it and a long narrow tail streamer (ButterflyModel.createBodyLayer, ButterflyModel.java:54-102). It drifts about the air on the butterfly flight preset (EntityButterfly.java:74; the vertical drag at tick :103-107 keeps it hovering), wears one of four skins (ButterflyRenderer.java:33-37), and an empty-handed right-click on it carries the player to the Chaos dimension and back (mobInteract, EntityButterfly.java:117-149). In the Islands its type-1 form hunts prey and nips for 1.0 on a 1-in-2 roll (doHurtTarget :161-165, reached from ButterflyIslandsHuntGoal.java:83). It spawns by day, in the air, above y 50 or anywhere in the Islands (checkSpawnRules :209-219), in forest, jungle and taiga swarms (the swarm_butterfly biome modifiers). Read it as a fluttering insect: everything is in the wings.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig (ButterflyRenderer has no scale override; shadow 0.3, ButterflyRenderer.java:28) on a 64x32 sheet (ButterflyModel.java:104), four skins by the synced butterfly type (ButterflyRenderer.java:33-37); 0.4 x 0.4 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:602-603). The wing panels are one unit thick: they read only from above and the side.

groups.name: wings
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) each way; the four left panels the negative of the four right panels
groups.plain: the eight wing panels flap about the body's long axis together, 45 degrees up and down, the left side mirroring the right; nothing else moves
groups.math: rightwing.zRot = rightwing2.zRot = rightwing3.zRot = rightwing4.zRot = cos(ageInTicks * 1.3 * 1.0) * pi * 0.25; leftwing*.zRot = -rightwing.zRot
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 x wingspeed 1.0 (two float multiplies, left to right): the natural period is 2 pi / 1.3 = 4.83 ticks

behaviour: One rhythm runs at all times: the eight wing panels roll about the body's long axis at 1.3 rad/tick (a 4.83-tick beat), 45 degrees each way, the left set mirroring the right (ButterflyModel.java:109-115). The body and the head are static; the walk position, the walking speed, the head angles and the entity's state play no part in the pose.

The flight itself is the entity's: the butterfly preset of AmbientFlightGoal steers the delta movement (EntityButterfly.java:74; ButterflyIslandsHuntGoal carries the Islands hunt in the same goal) and tick :103-107 damps the vertical speed to 0.6 each tick, so it hovers and drifts rather than falls. The model never banks, pitches or bobs the body with that motion.
The renderer draws the head, then the body, then the wing pairs inner to outer (renderToBuffer, ButterflyModel.java:119-130).

clips.note: ruled 2026-09-06, Q3 (a): the vanilla death flip stays; a creature whose JSON ships a `death` clip gets the clip-replaces-flip mode, designed when the first such clip arrives (the Queen's own death clip the precedent) - a `death` delivered here plays under the flip until then

wishlist: in `fly`: a slow bob and a slight roll of the body with the beat, so the flight reads as fluttering rather than a flat glide (the code moves only the wings: ButterflyModel.java:109-115)
in `idle`: wings slowly opening and closing as a settled butterfly's do, distinct from the airborne flap
in `attack`: a short dart forward for the Islands nip (EntityButterfly.java:161-165) — the strike is small; keep it quick
a tail-streamer lag: `leftwing4` / `rightwing4` trailing a few degrees behind the panels instead of rolling rigidly with them
